1af6669b0639.en: Here are the first fifty digits of pi, and the last ten of the first million. <bookmark mark='a'/> They came from this series, found by the brothers David and Gregory Chudnovsky in 1988, which adds about fourteen correct digits per term. <bookmark mark='b'/> Seventy thousand terms, summed exactly with whole numbers in plain Python on this machine, took sixteen seconds. The sum is the easy part. The hard part is multiplying numbers a million digits long, again and again.
1af6669b0639.zh: 这是圆周率的前五十位，以及前一百万位中的最后十位。<bookmark mark='a'/>它们来自这个级数，由丘德诺夫斯基兄弟戴维和格雷戈里在1988年发现，每一项大约增加十四位正确数字。<bookmark mark='b'/>七万项，在这台机器上用纯 Python 的整数精确求和，花了十六秒。求和是容易的部分。难的是把一百万位长的数一遍又一遍地相乘。

2ea07663a1d3.en: So how long does it take to multiply two numbers of a million digits? <bookmark mark='a'/> The way we learned at school, every digit times every digit, is a trillion small products: measured on smaller numbers and projected, about twenty-seven hours in Python. <bookmark mark='b'/> Python's own integers take under a second, because they use a trick found by a Moscow student in 1960. <bookmark mark='c'/> Python's decimal module is four times faster again, with a transform over a finite field. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the fast Fourier transform, the heart of this part, does the multiplication itself in four hundredths of a second. <bookmark mark='e'/> Same numbers, same answer: the difference is the idea.
2ea07663a1d3.zh: 那么，把两个一百万位的数相乘要多久？<bookmark mark='a'/>用我们在学校学的方法，每一位乘每一位，是一万亿次小乘法：在较小的数上测量后推算，用 Python 大约要二十七个小时。<bookmark mark='b'/>Python 自己的整数不到一秒，因为它用了一位莫斯科学生在1960年发现的技巧。<bookmark mark='c'/>Python 的 decimal 模块又快四倍，用的是有限域上的一种变换。<bookmark mark='d'/>而快速傅里叶变换，这一部分的核心，完成乘法本身只要百分之四秒。<bookmark mark='e'/>同样的数，同样的答案：差别在于思想。

f133e47165d6.en: Most good algorithms come from a handful of ideas, and this part names them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Greedy algorithms take the best-looking step each time; the work is in proving they never regret it, and knowing when they would. <bookmark mark='b'/> Divide and conquer splits a problem, solves the parts, and combines them; applied to the right points it gives the most important algorithm of the century. <bookmark mark='c'/> Dynamic programming solves every subproblem once, in an order where each answer is ready when it is needed. <bookmark mark='d'/> And when nothing cleverer is known, we search, trying choices and undoing them, as cleverly as possible.
f133e47165d6.zh: 大多数好的算法都来自少数几种思想，这一部分给它们命名。<bookmark mark='a'/>贪心算法每次走看起来最好的一步；功夫在于证明它从不后悔，并且知道它什么时候会后悔。<bookmark mark='b'/>分治把问题拆开，分别解决各部分，再合起来；用在合适的点上，它给出了二十世纪最重要的算法。<bookmark mark='c'/>动态规划把每个子问题只解一次，并按一种顺序进行，使每个答案在需要时已经备好。<bookmark mark='d'/>当没有更聪明的结构可用时，我们就搜索：尝试各种选择、撤销失败的选择，并尽可能聪明地做。

e41dc4148969.en: Part 19 of Computer Science, Built: The Great Paradigms. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: greedy algorithms and when they are right; multiplying numbers and matrices with fewer products; the fast Fourier transform, from scratch; dynamic programming in five settings; search, from the eight queens to Sudoku; one problem solved four ways; and the open questions about how fast we can multiply.
e41dc4148969.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第19部分：伟大的范式。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分讲：贪心算法以及它何时正确；用更少的乘法计算数与矩阵的乘积；从零推导快速傅里叶变换；五种情境下的动态规划；搜索，从八皇后到数独；用四种方法解决同一个问题；以及关于乘法能有多快的未解问题。

802986c07f33.en: Chapter one. Greedy, and the exchange argument.

8f9b7fb897e9.en: One lecture room, and requests for meetings, each with a start and an end. <bookmark mark='a'/> We want to fit in as many as possible without overlaps. <bookmark mark='b'/> A greedy rule: take the meeting that finishes first, discard everything that overlaps it, and repeat with what is left. The requests are sorted here by their finishing times. <bookmark mark='c'/> It chooses four meetings, and no schedule does better. <bookmark mark='d'/> One sort and one scan. But why should a rule that never looks ahead be optimal?
8f9b7fb897e9.zh: 一间报告厅，许多会议申请，每个都有开始和结束时间。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们想在不重叠的前提下安排尽可能多的会议。<bookmark mark='b'/>一条贪心规则：选最先结束的会议，删去与它重叠的一切，然后对剩下的重复。这里的申请按结束时间排好了序。<bookmark mark='c'/>它选出四个会议，没有任何安排能做得更好。<bookmark mark='d'/>一次排序，一次扫描。但一个从不往前看的规则，为什么会是最优的？

bc3028f97465.en: The proof is called an exchange argument. <bookmark mark='a'/> Greedy's first meeting finishes no later than any meeting at all. <bookmark mark='b'/> Take any best schedule and swap its first meeting for greedy's. Greedy's ends earlier, so it cannot clash with anything that came after; the schedule is still valid and just as large. <bookmark mark='c'/> So some best schedule begins with greedy's choice, and the rest of it is a best schedule for the meetings that start later, where the same argument applies. <bookmark mark='d'/> By induction, greedy is never behind. That is the shape of nearly every greedy proof: show that a best solution can be changed, one step at a time, into the greedy one without getting worse.
bc3028f97465.zh: 这个证明叫作交换论证。<bookmark mark='a'/>贪心选的第一个会议，结束得不晚于任何一个会议。<bookmark mark='b'/>任取一个最好的安排，把它的第一个会议换成贪心的那个。贪心的那个结束得更早，所以不会与后面的任何会议冲突；安排仍然合法，而且一样大。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以某个最好的安排是以贪心的选择开头的，它的其余部分是对较晚开始的会议的一个最好安排，同样的论证在那里也适用。<bookmark mark='d'/>由归纳法，贪心从不落后。这几乎是所有贪心证明的样子：证明一个最好的解可以一步一步地变成贪心的解，而不会变差。

98488f4bd77b.en: Without a proof, greedy is a gamble. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are four natural rules, each run on two thousand random sets of meetings. Finishing first is always right, as proved. Fewest overlaps is almost always right, and still wrong on a careful example of fifteen meetings. <bookmark mark='b'/> Shortest first fails on three meetings: it takes the short one in the middle and blocks two. Starting first fails often. <bookmark mark='c'/> Making change is the same story. With coins of one, three and four, greedy pays six as four plus one plus one, where three plus three is better, and it is wrong for a quarter of all amounts below a hundred. With American coins it is never wrong, and in 1994 Dexter Kozen and Shmuel Zaks showed that if greedy ever fails for a set of coins, it already fails on some amount below the two largest coins added together.
98488f4bd77b.zh: 没有证明，贪心就是一场赌博。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有四条自然的规则，每条都在两千组随机会议上运行。最先结束总是对的，已经证明。冲突最少几乎总是对的，但在一个精心构造的十五个会议的例子上仍然出错。<bookmark mark='b'/>最短优先在三个会议上就会失败：它选中中间那个短的，挡住了两个。最先开始则经常失败。<bookmark mark='c'/>找零钱也是同样的故事。硬币面值为一、三、四时，贪心把六付成四加一加一，而三加三更好，在一百以下的金额中，它有四分之一是错的。对美国硬币它从不出错，而1994年德克斯特·科森和什穆埃尔·扎克斯证明：如果贪心对某套硬币会出错，那它在小于两个最大面值之和的某个金额上就已经出错了。

f39060f61139.en: In 1952 David Huffman, a graduate student at MIT, was offered the choice of a final exam or a term paper, and solved a problem his professor, Robert Fano, had not. <bookmark mark='a'/> To build the shortest prefix code for a set of symbols, repeatedly merge the two rarest into one. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is greedy, and an exchange argument proves it: some best code tree has the two rarest symbols as the deepest pair of siblings, so merging them first loses nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the letters and spaces of our thirty novels, Huffman's code spends four point one two bits per symbol, against five for a fixed-length code: two bits for a space, four for e and t, ten for q and z. <bookmark mark='d'/> Shannon's entropy, the limit for any code that spends whole bits on each symbol in isolation, is four point zero eight. AI, Built's first part met this game.
f39060f61139.zh: 1952年，麻省理工学院的研究生戴维·哈夫曼可以在期末考试和学期论文之间选择，他解决了他的教授罗伯特·法诺没有解决的一个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>要为一组符号构造最短的前缀码，就反复把两个最稀有的符号合并成一个。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是贪心，一个交换论证证明了它：某棵最好的编码树中，两个最稀有的符号是最深的一对兄弟，所以先合并它们没有任何损失。<bookmark mark='c'/>在我们三十部小说的字母和空格上，哈夫曼码每个符号用四点一二比特，而定长码要五比特：空格两比特，e 和 t 四比特，q 和 z 十比特。<bookmark mark='d'/>香农熵，即对每个符号单独使用整数比特的任何编码的极限，是四点零八。AI，从零构建的第一部分玩过这个游戏。

bed1c6d48dc4.en: Chapter two. When greedy is right: matroids.
bed1c6d48dc4.zh: 第2章。贪心何时正确：拟阵。

62a3dcc956c2.en: In 1935 Hassler Whitney noticed that independence behaves the same way in very different places. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a ground set and call some of its subsets independent, with three rules. The empty set is independent. <bookmark mark='b'/> Any subset of an independent set is independent. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the exchange rule: if one independent set is smaller than another, it can always borrow some element of the larger one and stay independent. <bookmark mark='d'/> Linearly independent vectors obey these rules; that is where the name matroid comes from. <bookmark mark='e'/> So do the edge sets without cycles in a graph. Here the two blue edges form a forest, the three green edges a larger one, and the blue set can take a green edge without closing a cycle. <bookmark mark='f'/> And trivially, all sets of at most k elements.
62a3dcc956c2.zh: 1935年，哈斯勒·惠特尼注意到，独立性在非常不同的地方表现得一模一样。<bookmark mark='a'/>取一个基础集合，把它的某些子集称为独立的，满足三条规则。空集是独立的。<bookmark mark='b'/>独立集的任何子集都是独立的。<bookmark mark='c'/>还有交换规则：如果一个独立集比另一个小，它总能从大的那个借来某个元素而保持独立。<bookmark mark='d'/>线性无关的向量遵守这些规则；拟阵这个名字就来自那里。<bookmark mark='e'/>图中没有圈的边集也遵守。这里两条蓝边构成一个森林，三条绿边构成一个更大的森林，而蓝色集合可以拿走一条绿边而不闭合任何圈。<bookmark mark='f'/>还有最平凡的例子：所有至多 k 个元素的集合。

c39bb2868026.en: Here is why the definition matters. <bookmark mark='a'/> The greedy algorithm for a weighted set: consider elements heaviest first, and keep each one if the chosen set stays independent. <bookmark mark='b'/> Richard Rado in 1957, and Jack Edmonds in 1971, proved that greedy finds a heaviest independent set for every possible choice of weights exactly when the structure is a matroid. <bookmark mark='c'/> One direction is short. List greedy's choices and a best set's elements, each heaviest first. <bookmark mark='d'/> If at some position the best set's element were heavier, apply the exchange rule to greedy's first i minus one choices and the best set's first i: some element at least that heavy fits. <bookmark mark='e'/> Then greedy would have reached it before its i-th choice and taken it, a contradiction. <bookmark mark='f'/> Forests are a matroid, and this greedy is Kruskal's algorithm from Part 18. On four hundred random graphs, checked by brute force, it was optimal every time.
c39bb2868026.zh: 这个定义为什么重要？<bookmark mark='a'/>带权集合上的贪心算法：按从重到轻的顺序考察元素，如果加入后所选集合仍然独立，就保留它。<bookmark mark='b'/>理查德·拉多在1957年、杰克·埃德蒙兹在1971年证明了：对每一种可能的权值，贪心都能找到最重的独立集，当且仅当这个结构是拟阵。<bookmark mark='c'/>其中一个方向很短。把贪心的选择和一个最好集合的元素都按从重到轻列出来。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果在某个位置上，最好集合的元素更重，就对贪心的前 i 减一个选择和最好集合的前 i 个元素应用交换规则：有一个至少同样重的元素放得进去。<bookmark mark='e'/>那么贪心在做第 i 个选择之前就会遇到它并选中它，矛盾。<bookmark mark='f'/>森林是拟阵，这个贪心就是第18部分的克鲁斯卡尔算法。在四百个随机图上用穷举检验，它每次都是最优的。

04220b771376.en: And when the structure is not a matroid, greedy can be wrong. <bookmark mark='a'/> On this path, greedy takes the heaviest edge, three, and then nothing else fits. <bookmark mark='b'/> The two edges of weight two would have made four. Matchings break the exchange rule: the single middle edge cannot borrow either end edge. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the same four hundred random graphs, greedy matching was optimal only about three times in five, and once fell to sixty percent of the best. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is never worse than half, because each edge it takes can block at most two edges of a best matching. <bookmark mark='e'/> Exact maximum matching needs a cleverer idea, the augmenting paths of Part 18, which Edmonds also extended to general graphs in 1965.
04220b771376.zh: 而当结构不是拟阵时，贪心就可能出错。<bookmark mark='a'/>在这条路径上，贪心选了最重的边，三，然后就什么都放不进去了。<bookmark mark='b'/>两条权为二的边本可以凑成四。匹配违反了交换规则：单独的中间那条边借不到两端的任何一条。<bookmark mark='c'/>在同样的四百个随机图上，贪心匹配只有大约五分之三的时候是最优的，有一次只得到最好值的百分之六十。<bookmark mark='d'/>它从不差于一半，因为它选的每条边至多挡住一个最好匹配中的两条边。<bookmark mark='e'/>精确的最大匹配需要更聪明的思想，即第18部分的增广路径，埃德蒙兹在1965年也把它推广到了一般图。

bc9c3d810954.en: Chapter three. Three products instead of four.
bc9c3d810954.zh: 第3章。三次乘法代替四次。

716dd0621d20.en: In the autumn of 1960 Andrey Kolmogorov, one of the great mathematicians of the twentieth century, ran a seminar in Moscow on the complexity of arithmetic. <bookmark mark='a'/> He conjectured that multiplying two n digit numbers needs on the order of n squared steps, as it always had. <bookmark mark='b'/> Nobody doubted it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Within a week Anatoly Karatsuba, a twenty-three-year-old student, brought him a method that takes about n to the one point five eight. <bookmark mark='d'/> Kolmogorov was upset, announced the result at the next meeting, and ended the seminar. He wrote the paper himself, published under Karatsuba's name and Yuri Ofman's in 1962. <bookmark mark='e'/> It began the subject this part's opening table was about.
716dd0621d20.zh: 1960年秋天，二十世纪最伟大的数学家之一安德烈·柯尔莫哥洛夫在莫斯科主持了一个关于算术复杂性的讨论班。<bookmark mark='a'/>他猜想，两个 n 位数相乘需要 n 的平方量级的步数，一向如此。<bookmark mark='b'/>没有人怀疑。<bookmark mark='c'/>不到一周，二十三岁的学生阿纳托利·卡拉楚巴带来了一个大约需要 n 的一点五八次方的方法。<bookmark mark='d'/>柯尔莫哥洛夫很不高兴，在下一次讨论班上宣布了这个结果，并结束了讨论班。他亲自写了论文，以卡拉楚巴和尤里·奥夫曼的名义在1962年发表。<bookmark mark='e'/>它开启了这一部分开头那张表所讲的学科。

c0557ac436a6.en: Here is the trick. <bookmark mark='a'/> Split each number into a high half and a low half. <bookmark mark='b'/> The product needs four half-size products: high times high, low times low, and the two cross terms. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the two cross terms are only needed as a sum, and that sum is the product of the two half-sums, minus the two products we already have. Three multiplications instead of four, paid for with a few additions, which are cheap. <bookmark mark='d'/> For 1234 times 5678: twelve times fifty-six, thirty-four times seventy-eight, and forty-six times one hundred and thirty-four, from which the middle term follows by subtraction. Three products give seven million and six thousand, six hundred and fifty-two.
c0557ac436a6.zh: 技巧是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个数分成高半部分和低半部分。<bookmark mark='b'/>乘积需要四个半规模的乘法：高乘高、低乘低，以及两个交叉项。<bookmark mark='c'/>但两个交叉项只需要它们的和，而这个和等于两个半部分之和的乘积，减去我们已经算出的两个乘积。三次乘法代替四次，代价是几次加法，而加法很便宜。<bookmark mark='d'/>对 1234 乘 5678：十二乘五十六，三十四乘七十八，以及四十六乘一百三十四，中间项由减法得出。三次乘法给出七百万六千六百五十二。

bd82e8868a8b.en: The saving compounds. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each of the three half-size products is done the same way, so the work forms a tree: one product, then three, then nine, then twenty-seven, each half the size of the last. <bookmark mark='b'/> After log n levels there are three to the log n single-digit products, which is n to the log of three, about n to the one point five eight five. <bookmark mark='c'/> With four products per level the same tree would have n squared leaves. Saving one product in four at the top saves almost everything at the bottom: for four thousand digits, half a million digit products instead of sixteen million.
bd82e8868a8b.zh: 节省会层层累积。<bookmark mark='a'/>三个半规模的乘法各自用同样的方法计算，所以工作量构成一棵树：一个乘法，然后三个，然后九个，然后二十七个，每一层的规模都是上一层的一半。<bookmark mark='b'/>经过 log n 层，有三的 log n 次方个一位数乘法，也就是 n 的 log 三次方，大约 n 的一点五八五次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>若每层四次乘法，同一棵树会有 n 的平方片叶子。在顶层四次中省掉一次，在底层就几乎省掉了一切：四千位数时，是五十万次数字乘法，而不是一千六百万次。

3b8263ba1a27.en: Here it is measured, on digit lists in Python. <bookmark mark='a'/> The products fall as predicted, by a factor of thirty at four thousand digits. But the time does not, at first: recursing all the way down to single digits, Karatsuba is slower than the school method even at four thousand digits, because its additions, splits and function calls cost more than the products they save. <bookmark mark='b'/> The cure is a cutoff. Switch to the school method for pieces below thirty-two digits, and Karatsuba is ahead from sixty-four digits on, and almost four times faster at four thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> Python's own integers do exactly this, with a cutoff of seventy machine digits. <bookmark mark='d'/> Splitting into three pieces instead of two, Andrei Toom and Stephen Cook found five products where nine were needed, and the exponent fell again. The limit of the idea is the FFT.
3b8263ba1a27.zh: 这是用 Python 在数字列表上的实测。<bookmark mark='a'/>乘法次数如预言般下降，在四千位时少了三十倍。但时间起初并没有：一直递归到一位数，即使在四千位时 Karatsuba 也比学校方法慢，因为它的加法、拆分和函数调用的开销超过了省下的乘法。<bookmark mark='b'/>解药是截断阈值。片段小于三十二位时改用学校方法，Karatsuba 从六十四位起就领先，在四千位时快了近四倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>Python 自己的整数正是这样做的，阈值是七十个机器数位。<bookmark mark='d'/>把数分成三段而不是两段，安德烈·图姆和斯蒂芬·库克用五次乘法代替了本需的九次，指数又一次下降。这个思想的极限就是 FFT。

e2d04d49bd75.en: Chapter four. Seven products instead of eight.
e2d04d49bd75.zh: 第4章。七次乘法代替八次。

a03f5ee8d666.en: Nine years later Volker Strassen did the same to matrices, in a paper titled Gaussian elimination is not optimal. <bookmark mark='a'/> Split each matrix into four blocks. The product needs eight block products, two for each block of the answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> Strassen found seven products of sums and differences of blocks, coloured here, from which all four answer blocks follow by addition alone. <bookmark mark='c'/> They work because blocks need not commute: no step ever swaps the order of a product, so the identities hold for blocks, and the method recurses. <bookmark mark='d'/> Seven half-size products and some additions give n to the log of seven, about n to the two point eight one, against n cubed.
a03f5ee8d666.zh: 九年后，福尔克尔·施特拉森对矩阵做了同样的事，论文题为《高斯消元不是最优的》。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个矩阵分成四块。乘积需要八次块乘法，答案的每一块两次。<bookmark mark='b'/>施特拉森找到了七个由块的和与差组成的乘积，这里用颜色标出，答案的四块都能仅用加法从它们得出。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们之所以成立，是因为没有任何一步交换乘法的次序，而块不一定可交换：所以这些恒等式对块也成立，方法可以递归。<bookmark mark='d'/>七次半规模乘法加上一些加法，得到 n 的 log 七次方，大约 n 的二点八一次方，而不是 n 的立方。

43a83424effd.en: Counted exactly, all the way down to single numbers. <bookmark mark='a'/> At a thousand by a thousand, Strassen does a quarter as many multiplications, but one and a half times as many additions, eighteen block additions per level instead of four. <bookmark mark='b'/> Asymptotically the additions do not matter, since they are only n squared per level; but they show why the method pays only for large matrices, and why real implementations stop recursing long before single numbers.
43a83424effd.zh: 一直数到单个数字为止的精确计数。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一千乘一千时，施特拉森的乘法次数约为四分之一，但加法是一点五倍多，每层十八次块加法而不是四次。<bookmark mark='b'/>渐近地看加法无关紧要，因为每层只有 n 的平方；但它们说明了为什么这个方法只对大矩阵有利，以及为什么实际实现远在到达单个数字之前就停止递归。

a250f5ef3478.en: Strassen's paper started a race that is still going. <bookmark mark='a'/> Call omega the best exponent of matrix multiplication. <bookmark mark='b'/> Strassen brought it from three to two point eight one. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1990 Don Coppersmith and Shmuel Winograd reached two point three seven six, by a far more indirect method, and nothing moved for twenty years. <bookmark mark='d'/> Since 2010 a series of papers, most recently by Josh Alman, Ran Duan, Virginia Vassilevska Williams and three coauthors in 2024, have shaved it to two point three seven one three. <bookmark mark='e'/> The only lower bound is the obvious one, two: an answer has n squared entries to write. Many researchers suspect omega is two. <bookmark mark='f'/> None of the recent methods will ever run. Their constants are so large that they win only on matrices too big to exist, which Richard Lipton and Ken Regan call galactic algorithms.
a250f5ef3478.zh: 施特拉森的论文开启了一场至今仍在进行的竞赛。<bookmark mark='a'/>把矩阵乘法的最佳指数记作 omega。<bookmark mark='b'/>施特拉森把它从三降到了二点八一。<bookmark mark='c'/>1990年，唐·科珀史密斯和什穆埃尔·维诺格拉德用一种间接得多的方法达到了二点三七六，此后二十年纹丝不动。<bookmark mark='d'/>2010年以来，一系列论文，最近的是乔希·阿尔曼、段然、维尔吉尼娅·瓦西列夫斯卡·威廉斯和另外三位合作者在2024年的工作，把它削减到了二点三七一三。<bookmark mark='e'/>唯一的下界是显然的那个，二：答案有 n 的平方个元素要写。许多研究者猜测 omega 就是二。<bookmark mark='f'/>近年的这些方法永远不会真正运行。它们的常数大到只在大得不可能存在的矩阵上才占优，理查德·利普顿和肯·里甘把这类算法叫作银河算法。

8cd09ec97d7f.en: And in practice? <bookmark mark='a'/> We timed Strassen's recursion, handing blocks of two hundred and fifty-six to numpy, against numpy's own product. The tuned cubic method won at every size, by three to five times, because it uses the cache blocking, vector instructions and four cores of Parts 9 and 10, and does no extra additions. <bookmark mark='b'/> Strassen's subtractions also cost accuracy: in a test its rounding error was ten times larger. <bookmark mark='c'/> It is used where it pays, on very large matrices or exact arithmetic. <bookmark mark='d'/> The search for such schemes is not over. In 2022 DeepMind's AlphaTensor, a reinforcement learner, found a way to multiply four by four matrices with forty-seven products in arithmetic modulo two, where Strassen's method needs forty-nine.
8cd09ec97d7f.zh: 那么在实践中呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>我们把施特拉森的递归计时，把两百五十六大小的块交给 numpy，与 numpy 自己的乘法比较。经过调优的立方方法在每个规模上都赢了，快三到五倍，因为它用上了第9、10部分的缓存分块、向量指令和四个核心，而且不做额外的加法。<bookmark mark='b'/>施特拉森的减法还会损失精度：在一次测试中它的舍入误差大了十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>它用在划算的地方，即非常大的矩阵或精确算术。<bookmark mark='d'/>寻找这类方案的工作还没有结束。2022年，DeepMind 的强化学习系统 AlphaTensor 找到了一种在模二算术下用四十七次乘法计算四乘四矩阵乘积的方法，而施特拉森的方法需要四十九次。

c5d18661880c.en: Chapter five. The fast Fourier transform, part one: values instead of coefficients.
c5d18661880c.zh: 第5章。快速傅里叶变换（上）：用值代替系数。

4868963b0b69.en: Multiplying polynomials is the same problem as multiplying numbers, without the carries: a number is a polynomial evaluated at ten. <bookmark mark='a'/> Held as coefficients, two polynomials of n terms multiply in n squared steps, every coefficient times every other. <bookmark mark='b'/> But a polynomial can also be held as its values at enough points, and then multiplication is easy: the product's value at each point is just the product of the values. Two n steps, not n squared. <bookmark mark='c'/> Three points pin down a parabola, and in general n values pin down a polynomial below degree n. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the plan is: evaluate, multiply pointwise, and interpolate back. <bookmark mark='e'/> The catch is the evaluation. At arbitrary points, each value costs n steps, and we are back to n squared. Everything depends on choosing the points.
4868963b0b69.zh: 多项式相乘与整数相乘是同一个问题，只是没有进位：一个数就是一个多项式在十处的取值。<bookmark mark='a'/>用系数表示时，两个 n 项的多项式相乘需要 n 的平方步，每个系数乘每个系数。<bookmark mark='b'/>但多项式也可以用它在足够多个点上的值来表示，这时乘法很容易：乘积在每个点上的值，就是两个值的乘积。二 n 步，而不是 n 的平方。<bookmark mark='c'/>三个点确定一条抛物线，一般地，n 个值确定一个次数低于 n 的多项式。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以计划是：求值，逐点相乘，再插值回来。<bookmark mark='e'/>难点在于求值。在任意的点上，每个值要花 n 步，我们又回到了 n 的平方。一切取决于怎样选点。

ddbb9fa315ef.en: Here is the idea. <bookmark mark='a'/> Split a polynomial into its even and odd terms. Both halves are polynomials in x squared, of half the degree. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now evaluate at a pair of opposite points, plus x and minus x. <bookmark mark='c'/> The halves see the same input, x squared, so the two values share all their work and differ only in a sign. <bookmark mark='d'/> Choosing the points in plus–minus pairs halves the work at the top level. <bookmark mark='e'/> To repeat the trick, the halves must be evaluated at the squares, half as many points, and those squares must themselves come in plus–minus pairs. <bookmark mark='f'/> But a square of a real number is never negative. Real numbers cannot do it.
ddbb9fa315ef.zh: 思路是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>把多项式分成偶次项和奇次项。两半都是 x 平方的多项式，次数减半。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在在一对相反的点，正 x 和负 x 上求值。<bookmark mark='c'/>两半看到的输入相同，都是 x 平方，所以两个值共享全部工作，只差一个符号。<bookmark mark='d'/>成对地选取正负点，就把顶层的工作减半了。<bookmark mark='e'/>要重复这个技巧，两半需要在这些平方上求值，点数减半，而且这些平方本身也必须成正负对出现。<bookmark mark='f'/>但实数的平方永远不是负数。实数做不到。

c53f07aafc0c.en: Complex numbers can. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the eight points equally spaced around the unit circle: the eighth roots of unity, the numbers whose eighth power is one. <bookmark mark='b'/> They come in opposite pairs: rotating by half a turn negates a point. <bookmark mark='c'/> Squaring a point on the circle doubles its angle. Watch what happens to all eight: opposite points land together, and the eight become the four fourth roots of unity. <bookmark mark='d'/> Those four are again two opposite pairs. Square again: two points, plus one and minus one. Square once more, and everything lands on one. At every level the points pair up, exactly as the recursion needs. <bookmark mark='e'/> So evaluating at the n-th roots of unity takes two half-size evaluations plus linear work: n log n. That evaluation is the discrete Fourier transform, and this way of computing it is the fast Fourier transform.
c53f07aafc0c.zh: 复数可以。<bookmark mark='a'/>取单位圆上等距分布的八个点：八次单位根，即八次方等于一的那些数。<bookmark mark='b'/>它们成对相反：旋转半圈会把一个点变成它的相反数。<bookmark mark='c'/>把圆上的点平方，就是把它的角度加倍。看看八个点都会怎样：相反的点落到一起，八个点变成了四个四次单位根。<bookmark mark='d'/>这四个点又是两对相反的点。再平方：两个点，正一和负一。再平方一次，一切都落到一上。每一层，点都恰好像递归需要的那样成对。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以在 n 次单位根上求值，只需两个半规模的求值加上线性的工作：n log n。这个求值就是离散傅里叶变换，而这种计算方法就是快速傅里叶变换。

898dbcc0c818.en: Here is the whole algorithm. <bookmark mark='a'/> Transform the even coefficients and the odd ones, recursively. Then, for each k in the first half, multiply the odd value by a root of unity, called a twiddle factor, and add and subtract: that gives two outputs at once. Ten lines, n log n time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Going back is almost free: the inverse transform is the same algorithm run with the inverse root, then divided by n. The next chapter shows why. <bookmark mark='c'/> Evaluate both factors, multiply pointwise, transform back: polynomials, and with care integers, multiply in n log n.
898dbcc0c818.zh: 这就是整个算法。<bookmark mark='a'/>递归地变换偶数位置和奇数位置的系数。然后对前一半的每个 k，把奇数部分的值乘以一个单位根，叫作旋转因子，再相加和相减：一次得到两个输出。十行代码，n log n 时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>反变换几乎是免费的：它是同一个算法，用单位根的倒数运行，再除以 n。下一章会说明为什么。<bookmark mark='c'/>对两个因子求值，逐点相乘，再变换回来：多项式，以及小心处理后的整数，都能在 n log n 内相乘。

aab22cb75b67.en: Chapter six. The fast Fourier transform, part two: butterflies.
aab22cb75b67.zh: 第6章。快速傅里叶变换（下）：蝶形。

8b4dd6c33c40.en: The algorithm was found twice. <bookmark mark='a'/> Around 1805 Carl Friedrich Gauss, fitting the orbits of the newly found asteroids Pallas and Juno, split his trigonometric sums in exactly this way. He never published it; it appeared after his death, in Latin, and was forgotten. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 1963 the statistician John Tukey, sitting on President Kennedy's science advisory committee, sketched the idea to Richard Garwin of IBM. <bookmark mark='c'/> Garwin wanted it for a pressing reason: to detect Soviet nuclear tests from seismometer recordings, which meant Fourier transforms of long signals, quickly. <bookmark mark='d'/> He had James Cooley program it, and Cooley and Tukey's paper of 1965 became one of the most cited in mathematics. <bookmark mark='e'/> In 1984 Michael Heideman, Don Johnson and Sidney Burrus found Gauss's version in his collected works.
8b4dd6c33c40.zh: 这个算法被发现了两次。<bookmark mark='a'/>1805年前后，卡尔·弗里德里希·高斯在拟合新发现的小行星智神星和婚神星的轨道时，正是这样拆分他的三角和的。他从未发表；它在他死后以拉丁文出版，随即被遗忘。<bookmark mark='b'/>1963年，统计学家约翰·图基在肯尼迪总统的科学顾问委员会上，向 IBM 的理查德·加温勾勒了这个想法。<bookmark mark='c'/>加温急需它：要从地震仪记录中探测苏联的核试验，这意味着要快速地对很长的信号做傅里叶变换。<bookmark mark='d'/>他让詹姆斯·库利编了程序，库利和图基1965年的论文成为数学中被引用最多的论文之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>1984年，迈克尔·海德曼、唐·约翰逊和西德尼·伯勒斯在高斯的全集中找到了他的版本。

2bd9cc35ca17.en: Unroll the recursion and it becomes a network. <bookmark mark='a'/> The recursion splits by the last bit of the index first, then the next, so the inputs arrive in bit-reversed order: index one, binary zero zero one, sits where four, one zero zero, would. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then come log n stages. In each, pairs of values are combined by a butterfly: one multiplication by a twiddle factor, one addition, one subtraction. The first stage pairs neighbours, the next pairs at distance two, then four. <bookmark mark='c'/> n over two butterflies per stage, log n stages, and every value is overwritten in place, so the transform needs no extra memory. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is the same wiring as the sorting networks and parallel prefix of Part 10, which is why FFTs run so well on parallel hardware.
2bd9cc35ca17.zh: 把递归展开，它就变成一个网络。<bookmark mark='a'/>递归先按下标的最低位拆分，再按下一位，所以输入按位反转的顺序排列：下标一，二进制零零一，位于四，即一零零，应在的位置。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是 log n 级。每一级里，成对的值由一个蝶形组合：一次乘以旋转因子，一次加法，一次减法。第一级配对相邻的，下一级配对相距二的，再下一级相距四。<bookmark mark='c'/>每级 n 除以二个蝶形，共 log n 级，每个值都就地覆盖，所以变换不需要额外内存。<bookmark mark='d'/>这和第10部分的排序网络与并行前缀是同样的连线，这就是 FFT 在并行硬件上跑得如此之好的原因。

98aabbbe9b11.en: Why is the inverse so cheap? <bookmark mark='a'/> Write the transform as a matrix whose entries are powers of omega. <bookmark mark='b'/> Multiply a row of it by a conjugated row. If the rows are the same, every term is one and the sum is n. If not, the terms are the powers of some root of unity other than one, spread evenly around the circle, and they cancel to zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the matrix's inverse is its own conjugate divided by n, the rows are orthogonal, and transforming back is the same fast algorithm with omega replaced by its inverse. <bookmark mark='d'/> This orthogonality of characters is the algebraic heart of Fourier analysis, from Analysis, Built's ninth part to Part 53's quantum computers.
98aabbbe9b11.zh: 为什么反变换这么便宜？<bookmark mark='a'/>把变换写成一个矩阵，其元素是 omega 的幂。<bookmark mark='b'/>把它的一行与另一行的共轭相乘。如果两行相同，每一项都是一，和为 n。否则，各项是某个不等于一的单位根的幂，均匀分布在圆周上，相互抵消为零。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以这个矩阵的逆就是它自己的共轭除以 n，各行相互正交，而变换回去就是把 omega 换成它的倒数的同一个快速算法。<bookmark mark='d'/>这种特征的正交性是傅里叶分析的代数核心，从分析，从零构建的第九部分，一直到第53部分的量子计算机。

2664bb818b1c.en: Measured on this machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> The direct transform does n squared multiplications, the fast one n over two log n butterflies. At two thousand points, written in the same plain Python, they agree to ten decimal places and the fast one is almost three hundred times faster. <bookmark mark='b'/> Numpy's compiled FFT transforms four million points in under half a second. <bookmark mark='c'/> It runs inside every phone call, every compressed photograph, every MRI scan and every Wi-Fi packet, which is why it is often called the most important algorithm of the twentieth century.
2664bb818b1c.zh: 在这台机器上实测。<bookmark mark='a'/>直接变换做 n 的平方次乘法，快速变换做 n 除以二乘 log n 个蝶形。在两千个点上，用同样的纯Python 编写，两者在小数点后十位上一致，而快速变换快了近三百倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>numpy 编译好的 FFT 在不到半秒内变换四百万个点。<bookmark mark='c'/>它运行在每一通电话、每一张压缩的照片、每一次核磁共振扫描和每一个 Wi-Fi 数据包里，这就是它常被称为二十世纪最重要算法的原因。

2df1fb0f5312.en: Chapter seven. What the FFT multiplies.

339cc2d019d4.en: To multiply integers, treat them as polynomials. <bookmark mark='a'/> Three hundred and twenty-one is one plus two x plus three x squared, at x equals ten. <bookmark mark='b'/> Multiply the polynomials, by the FFT for long ones, and the coefficients come out as four, thirteen, twenty-two and fifteen. <bookmark mark='c'/> They are too big to be digits, so carry: the result is seventeen thousand, three hundred and thirty-four, which is three hundred and twenty-one times fifty-four. <bookmark mark='d'/> In practice digits are grouped in blocks of four, transformed, multiplied pointwise and transformed back; then the results are rounded to whole numbers and the carries propagated.
339cc2d019d4.zh: 要把整数相乘，就把它们当作多项式。<bookmark mark='a'/>三百二十一就是一加二 x 加三 x 平方，在 x 等于十处的值。<bookmark mark='b'/>把多项式相乘，长的用 FFT，系数就是四、十三、二十二和十五。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们太大，不能当数字，所以要进位：结果是一万七千三百三十四，正是三百二十一乘以五十四。<bookmark mark='d'/>实践中数字按四位一组，变换，逐点相乘，再变换回来；然后把结果舍入为整数，并传递进位。

ce67c5d962df.en: Floating-point arithmetic is approximate, so is the answer right? <bookmark mark='a'/> Each coefficient of the true product is a whole number, so rounding gives it exactly as long as the accumulated error stays below one half. We measured the worst error over the whole product. <bookmark mark='b'/> It grows with the length, about tenfold for every tenfold here. <bookmark mark='c'/> At ten million digits it is five hundredths, comfortably safe, and the transforms take a little over a second. Much further, and the error would reach one half. Then one uses smaller digit blocks, or abandons floating point altogether.
ce67c5d962df.zh: 浮点运算是近似的，那么答案对吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>真实乘积的每个系数都是整数，所以只要累积误差保持在二分之一以下，舍入就能精确得到它。我们测量了整个乘积上的最大误差。<bookmark mark='b'/>它随长度增长，这里大约长度每增十倍误差也增十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>在一千万位时误差是百分之五，十分安全，变换只花一秒多一点。再大得多，误差就会达到二分之一。那时要用更小的数字分组，或者完全放弃浮点数。

4b2b74e05326.en: There is an exact version. <bookmark mark='a'/> Work modulo a prime such as this one, one hundred and nineteen times two to the twenty-three, plus one. <bookmark mark='b'/> In that arithmetic there are roots of unity too: suitable powers of three behave exactly like the points on the circle, squaring onto each other in pairs. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the same butterflies run on whole numbers, with nothing to round. This is the number-theoretic transform, and Part 30 will use it again for cryptography. <bookmark mark='d'/> Python's decimal module multiplies huge numbers this way. On short numbers it is slower than Python's Karatsuba integers; at a hundred thousand digits the two are level; at a million digits it is four times faster, and the gap keeps widening.
4b2b74e05326.zh: 还有一个精确的版本。<bookmark mark='a'/>在模一个素数下运算，比如这个：一百一十九乘以二的二十三次方，再加一。<bookmark mark='b'/>在这种算术里也有单位根：三的适当次幂表现得和圆上的点完全一样，成对地平方到彼此身上。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以同样的蝶形可以在整数上运行，没有任何需要舍入的东西。这就是数论变换，第30部分会在密码学中再次用到它。<bookmark mark='d'/>Python 的 decimal 模块就是这样做大数乘法的。对短的数，它比 Python 的 Karatsuba 整数慢；在十万位时两者持平；在一百万位时它快了四倍，而且差距还在扩大。

59a427afe983.en: Here is the whole history of multiplication. <bookmark mark='a'/> The school method, then Karatsuba and Toom and Cook. In 1971 Arnold Schönhage and Volker Strassen made the FFT exact over cleverly chosen rings, reaching n log n log log n, and conjectured that n log n was the truth. Martin Fürer came closer in 2007. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2019 David Harvey and Joris van der Hoeven proved n log n, forty-eight years after the conjecture. Most experts believe nothing faster is possible, though no one can prove it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our million digits of pi took sixteen seconds; the record, over two hundred trillion digits in 2024, was computed with the same ideas, on a much larger computer.
59a427afe983.zh: 这就是乘法的全部历史。<bookmark mark='a'/>学校方法，然后是 Karatsuba、图姆和库克。1971年，阿诺尔德·舍恩哈格和福尔克尔·施特拉森在巧妙选择的环上让 FFT 变得精确，达到 n log n log log n，并猜想 n log n 才是真相。马丁·菲雷尔在2007年更近了一步。<bookmark mark='b'/>2019年，戴维·哈维和约里斯·范德霍文证明了 n log n，距离那个猜想已经四十八年。大多数专家相信不可能更快，尽管没人能证明。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们的一百万位圆周率花了十六秒；而纪录，2024年的超过两百万亿位，用的是同样的思想，只是计算机大得多。

288073a3b499.en: Given a million points, which two are closest? Comparing every pair is half a trillion distances. <bookmark mark='a'/> Michael Shamos and Dan Hoey's divide and conquer, from 1975: sort the points from left to right and split them at the median. <bookmark mark='b'/> Find the closest pair on each side, recursively. <bookmark mark='c'/> Call the smaller of the two distances delta. Any pair closer than delta must have one point on each side of the line. <bookmark mark='d'/> And both of its points must lie within delta of the line, in a thin strip.
288073a3b499.zh: 给定一百万个点，哪两个最近？比较每一对要算五千亿个距离。<bookmark mark='a'/>迈克尔·沙莫斯和丹·霍伊1975年的分治法：把点从左到右排序，在中位数处分开。<bookmark mark='b'/>递归地求出每一边的最近点对。<bookmark mark='c'/>把两个距离中较小的记作 delta。任何比delta 更近的点对都必须一个点在分界线左边，一个在右边。<bookmark mark='d'/>而且它的两个点都必须在离分界线 delta 以内，在一条窄带里。

7f342682a736.en: The strip could hold almost every point, so why is it cheap? <bookmark mark='a'/> Sort the strip's points from bottom to top, and compare each point only with the points above it, less than delta higher. <bookmark mark='b'/> Those all lie in a box two delta wide and delta high, which cuts into eight squares of side delta over two. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each square lies on one side of the line, and any two points in it would be less than delta apart, closer than the best pair on that side. So each square holds at most one point. <bookmark mark='d'/> Hence each point needs at most seven comparisons, and the strip costs linear time. <bookmark mark='e'/> Two half-size problems and linear work: n log n, by the same recurrence as merge sort and the FFT.
7f342682a736.zh: 窄带里可能有几乎所有的点，那为什么它很便宜？<bookmark mark='a'/>把窄带里的点从下到上排序，每个点只与它上方、高度差小于 delta 的点比较。<bookmark mark='b'/>这些点都落在一个宽二 delta、高 delta 的方框里，方框可切成八个边长为 delta 的一半的小正方形。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个小正方形都位于分界线的某一侧，其中任意两点的距离都小于 delta，比那一侧最好的点对还近。所以每个小正方形至多有一个点。<bookmark mark='d'/>因此每个点至多需要七次比较，窄带只花线性时间。<bookmark mark='e'/>两个半规模的问题加线性工作：n log n，与归并排序和 FFT 是同一个递推式。

edbaa66146d6.en: On random points, the counts tell the story. <bookmark mark='a'/> At a hundred thousand points, all pairs would be five billion distances; divide and conquer computed a hundred and forty-two thousand. In practice no point ever needed more than two comparisons in a strip; seven is only the worst case. <bookmark mark='b'/> It took a little over a second, where all pairs would take a quarter of an hour. <bookmark mark='c'/> Michael Rabin showed in 1976 that randomness does better still, expected linear time, by hashing points into grid cells of the right size.
edbaa66146d6.zh: 在随机点上，计数说明了一切。<bookmark mark='a'/>十万个点时，所有点对是五十亿个距离；分治法算了十四万二千个。实际上窄带里没有一个点需要超过两次比较；七只是最坏情况。<bookmark mark='b'/>它花了一秒多一点，而计算所有点对要一刻钟。<bookmark mark='c'/>迈克尔·拉宾在1976年证明了随机性能做得更好，期望线性时间，方法是把点散列到大小合适的网格单元中。

a4b4905b0ff1.en: The name is a piece of camouflage. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the 1950s Richard Bellman worked at the RAND Corporation on decisions taken in many stages. <bookmark mark='b'/> RAND was funded through the Air Force, and according to Bellman's autobiography the Secretary of Defense, Charles Wilson, had a horror of the word research, let alone mathematical. <bookmark mark='c'/> So Bellman chose programming, which then meant planning, as in a training programme, and dynamic, because, he wrote, it is impossible to use the word dynamic in a pejorative sense. <bookmark mark='d'/> The idea behind the name: an optimal plan is made of optimal plans for smaller problems, so solve the smaller problems first and remember the answers.
a4b4905b0ff1.zh: 这个名字是一种伪装。<bookmark mark='a'/>20世纪50年代，理查德·贝尔曼在兰德公司研究多阶段决策。<bookmark mark='b'/>兰德的经费来自空军，而据贝尔曼的自传，国防部长查尔斯·威尔逊对“研究”这个词深恶痛绝，更不用说“数学”了。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是贝尔曼选了“规划”，当时的意思是计划，就像训练计划；又选了“动态”，因为，他写道，不可能用贬义来使用“动态”这个词。<bookmark mark='d'/>名字背后的思想：最优计划由较小问题的最优计划组成，所以先解决较小的问题，并记住答案。

e210a5d913c5.en: The simplest example is the Fibonacci numbers, each the sum of the two before. <bookmark mark='a'/> Computed by plain recursion, F of five calls F of four and F of three, and F of four calls F of three again. The same subproblems are solved over and over: F of three twice, F of two three times. <bookmark mark='b'/> The number of calls grows like the golden ratio to the n, as fast as the answer itself. F of thirty takes two point seven million calls, half a second in Python. <bookmark mark='c'/> Remember each answer the first time it is computed, and F of thirty takes fifty-nine calls. That is memoization: the recursion stays, top-down, with a cache. <bookmark mark='d'/> Or turn it around and fill a table from the bottom up, in an order where everything needed is already there. That is tabulation, and it is what most dynamic programmes look like.
e210a5d913c5.zh: 最简单的例子是斐波那契数，每一个都是前两个之和。<bookmark mark='a'/>用朴素递归计算，F(5) 调用 F(4) 和 F(3)，而 F(4) 又调用 F(3)。同样的子问题被一遍又一遍地求解：F(3) 两次，F(2) 三次。<bookmark mark='b'/>调用次数像黄金分割比的 n 次方那样增长，和答案本身一样快。F(30) 要两百七十万次调用，在 Python 中半秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个答案第一次算出时就记住它，F(30) 只要五十九次调用。这就是记忆化：递归保留，自顶向下，加一个缓存。<bookmark mark='d'/>或者反过来，自底向上填一张表，顺序使得需要的一切都已经在那里。这就是制表法，大多数动态规划都长这个样子。

165fd42c610d.en: There is a picture behind every dynamic programme. <bookmark mark='a'/> Make each subproblem a vertex and draw an edge from each subproblem to every one that uses it. Because nothing can depend on itself, the graph has no cycles. <bookmark mark='b'/> Tabulation is just visiting this graph in topological order, the algorithm of Part 18's fourth chapter. <bookmark mark='c'/> For optimization problems, where each subproblem takes the best of several options, the answer is a shortest or longest path through this graph. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the running time is always the number of subproblems times the work each one does. The art is choosing subproblems: few enough, but enough to build on.
165fd42c610d.zh: 每个动态规划背后都有一幅图。<bookmark mark='a'/>把每个子问题作为顶点，从每个子问题向使用它的每个子问题连一条边。因为没有东西能依赖它自己，这张图没有圈。<bookmark mark='b'/>制表法就是按拓扑顺序访问这张图，即第18部分第4章的算法。<bookmark mark='c'/>对优化问题，每个子问题在几个选项中取最好的，答案就是这张图中的一条最短或最长路径。<bookmark mark='d'/>运行时间总是子问题的个数乘以每个子问题的工作量。艺术在于选择子问题：足够少，又足以在其上建立答案。

8f77596f93a4.en: How far apart are two strings? <bookmark mark='a'/> Vladimir Levenshtein in 1965 counted the fewest single-character edits, insertions, deletions and substitutions, that turn one into the other. <bookmark mark='b'/> The subproblems: the distance between the first i letters of one string and the first j of the other. <bookmark mark='c'/> Consider the last letters. Either the last letter of the first string is deleted, or the last letter of the second is inserted, or one is substituted for the other, which is free if they match. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nothing else can happen to them, so the best edit is the best of these three, each built on a smaller subproblem. <bookmark mark='e'/> There are n times m subproblems with constant work each.
8f77596f93a4.zh: 两个字符串相距多远？<bookmark mark='a'/>弗拉基米尔·莱文斯坦在1965年数的是把一个变成另一个所需的最少单字符编辑：插入、删除和替换。<bookmark mark='b'/>子问题：一个字符串的前 i 个字母与另一个的前 j 个字母之间的距离。<bookmark mark='c'/>考虑最后的字母。要么第一个字符串的最后一个字母被删除，要么第二个的最后一个字母被插入，要么一个被替换成另一个，若它们相同则不花代价。<bookmark mark='d'/>它们不可能有别的遭遇，所以最好的编辑就是这三者中最好的，每个都建立在一个更小的子问题上。<bookmark mark='e'/>共有 n 乘 m 个子问题，每个常数工作量。

dc46019b299c.en: Here is the table for intention and execution, a classic example. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first row and column count the cost of building a prefix from nothing. Every other cell takes the minimum of its three neighbours, so the table fills row by row, each cell ready when it is needed. <bookmark mark='b'/> The bottom-right corner holds the answer: five. <bookmark mark='c'/> To recover the edits themselves, walk back from the corner, each time to a neighbour that could have produced the value. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here the path runs down the diagonal: five substitutions, and the final four letters, t i o n, kept.
dc46019b299c.zh: 这是 intention 和 execution 的表，一个经典的例子。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一行和第一列计算从空串构造一个前缀的代价。其余每个格子取它三个邻居的最小值，所以表格一行一行地填，每个格子在需要时都已就绪。<bookmark mark='b'/>右下角的格子就是答案：五。<bookmark mark='c'/>要恢复编辑本身，就从这个角往回走，每次走到一个能产生当前值的邻居。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里路径沿着对角线：五次替换，最后四个字母 t、i、o、n 保留。

a10e8683aefe.en: Measured on random DNA strings in Python, the table is quadratic: <bookmark mark='a'/> doubling the length quadruples the time, and two thousand letters each take under three seconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Drop substitutions and count matches instead, and the same table finds the longest common subsequence. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is how diff and git compare files: line by line, the lines outside the common subsequence are the changes, as Parts 21 and 41 will show. <bookmark mark='d'/> In biology, Saul Needleman and Christian Wunsch used the same recurrence in 1970 to align proteins. <bookmark mark='e'/> It also runs spelling correctors and speech recognizers. And as the frontier chapter explains, there is good reason to think quadratic time cannot be beaten.
a10e8683aefe.zh: 在随机 DNA 字符串上用 Python 测量，这张表是平方的：<bookmark mark='a'/>长度加倍，时间变成四倍，两千个字母各自不到三秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>去掉替换、改为计数匹配，同一张表就能求出最长公共子序列。<bookmark mark='c'/>diff 和 git 就是这样比较文件的：逐行比较，公共子序列之外的行就是改动，第21和41部分会讲到。<bookmark mark='d'/>在生物学中，索尔·尼德曼和克里斯蒂安·温施在1970年用同一个递推式比对蛋白质。<bookmark mark='e'/>它还运行在拼写纠正器和语音识别器里。而正如前沿一章所解释的，有充分的理由认为平方时间无法被打破。

0f45975610cc.en: Chapter eleven. Knapsack, and pseudo-polynomial time.
0f45975610cc.zh: 第11章。背包问题与伪多项式时间。

45b82a3b7792.en: A thief with a knapsack that holds twelve kilograms faces six items, each with a weight and a value. <bookmark mark='a'/> The subproblem: the best value using only the first i items with capacity c. Either item i is left out, or it is taken, using up its weight. <bookmark mark='b'/> The table fills one item at a time; each row needs only the row above. <bookmark mark='c'/> The bottom-right cell is the answer, a hundred and ten, and tracing back through the cells where the value changed finds the items: weights three, two and seven, exactly filling the knapsack.
45b82a3b7792.zh: 一个小偷的背包能装十二公斤，面前有六件物品，每件有重量和价值。<bookmark mark='a'/>子问题：只用前 i 件物品、容量为 c 时的最大价值。第 i 件要么不拿，要么拿走并占用它的重量。<bookmark mark='b'/>表格一次填一件物品；每一行只需要上一行。<bookmark mark='c'/>右下角的格子就是答案，一百一十，沿着价值发生变化的格子往回追溯，就找到了物品：重量三、二和七，恰好装满背包。

3954281755a0.en: Why not be greedy? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take items in order of value per kilogram, as long as they fit. <bookmark mark='b'/> On our six items that gives a hundred and five, not a hundred and ten. <bookmark mark='c'/> On five hundred random sets of fifteen items it was wrong two times in five, once getting only seventy-eight percent of the best value. <bookmark mark='d'/> The independent sets here are not a matroid. If items could be cut, like gold dust, the same greedy would be exactly right: the fractional knapsack is a different, easier problem.
3954281755a0.zh: 为什么不贪心？<bookmark mark='a'/>按每公斤价值的顺序拿物品，只要放得下。<bookmark mark='b'/>在我们的六件物品上，这给出一百零五，而不是一百一十。<bookmark mark='c'/>在五百组随机的十五件物品上，它有五分之二的时候是错的，有一次只得到最好价值的百分之七十八。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里的独立集不是拟阵。如果物品能像金粉一样切开，同样的贪心就完全正确：分数背包是另一个更容易的问题。

592156373a5f.en: The table has n times W cells, which sounds polynomial. It is not. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are the same twenty items five times over, with every weight and the capacity multiplied by ten each time. The problem and its answer never change. <bookmark mark='b'/> But each step adds about three bits to the input and multiplies the work by ten: from a third of a millisecond to nearly five seconds. Time proportional to the capacity is exponential in the number of digits used to write it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Such an algorithm is called pseudo-polynomial: fast when the numbers are small. <bookmark mark='d'/> No truly polynomial algorithm is known, and Richard Karp proved in 1972 that none exists unless P equals NP, the subject of Part 26. Yet Oscar Ibarra and Chul Kim showed in 1975 that a solution within any fixed percentage of the best can be found in polynomial time.
592156373a5f.zh: 表格有 n 乘 W 个格子，听起来是多项式的。其实不是。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是同样的二十件物品，重复五次，每次把每件的重量和容量都乘以十。问题和答案从未改变。<bookmark mark='b'/>但每一步输入只多大约三个比特，工作量却乘以十：从三分之一毫秒到将近五秒。与容量成正比的时间，对写出容量所用的位数而言是指数的。<bookmark mark='c'/>这样的算法叫作伪多项式的：数字小时很快。<bookmark mark='d'/>没有已知的真正多项式算法，理查德·卡普在1972年证明，除非 P 等于 NP，否则不存在这样的算法，这是第26部分的主题。然而奥斯卡·伊瓦拉和 Chul Kim 在1975年证明，在多项式时间内可以找到与最优相差任意固定百分比以内的解。

03a93fd879cf.en: Chapter twelve. Matrix chains and optimal search trees.
03a93fd879cf.zh: 第12章。矩阵链与最优搜索树。

9082a9a1f398.en: Matrix multiplication is associative, so a product of six matrices can be bracketed in any order with the same answer, but not the same cost. <bookmark mark='a'/> Multiplying p by q by q by r takes p q r scalar products. <bookmark mark='b'/> For these six, from the standard textbook example, multiplying left to right costs forty thousand five hundred products, and the worst of the forty-two possible orders costs fifty-eight thousand. <bookmark mark='c'/> The subproblems are the contiguous runs from i to j. For each, try every place for the last multiplication, and add the best costs of the two sides. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is the recurrence. <bookmark mark='e'/> The best order costs fifteen thousand one hundred and twenty-five, about a quarter of the worst. <bookmark mark='f'/> The table has n squared entries with n choices each: cubic time, where the number of orders grows exponentially. Compilers and query planners face the same problem, choosing the order of joins in Part 35's databases.
9082a9a1f398.zh: 矩阵乘法满足结合律，所以六个矩阵的乘积可以任意加括号，答案相同，但代价不同。<bookmark mark='a'/>p 乘 q 的矩阵乘以 q 乘 r 的矩阵，要做 p 乘 q 乘 r 次标量乘法。<bookmark mark='b'/>对这六个矩阵，来自标准教科书的例子，从左到右相乘要四万零五百次乘法，而四十二种可能顺序中最差的要五万八千次。<bookmark mark='c'/>子问题是从 i 到 j 的连续一段。对每一段，尝试最后一次乘法的每个位置，并加上两边的最好代价。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是递推式。<bookmark mark='e'/>最好的顺序代价是一万五千一百二十五，约为最差的四分之一。<bookmark mark='f'/>表格有 n 的平方个元素，每个 n 种选择：立方时间，而顺序的数目是指数增长的。编译器和查询规划器面临同样的问题，即在第35部分的数据库中选择连接的顺序。

b84a29a6bcb8.en: A cousin of this problem goes back to Part 17. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose we know how often each key will be looked up. Which binary search tree minimizes the expected search cost? Frequent keys should be near the root, but the tree must stay ordered. <bookmark mark='b'/> The recurrence has the same shape: for every range of keys, try every key as the root. Cubic time. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1971 Donald Knuth proved that the best root of a range never moves left when the range grows on the right, and never right when it grows on the left. <bookmark mark='d'/> So each range needs to try only the roots between two neighbours' answers, and the total falls to quadratic. <bookmark mark='e'/> At two hundred keys, the same answer in thirty-three times fewer steps. The inequality behind it, later called the quadrangle inequality, speeds up many other dynamic programmes.
b84a29a6bcb8.zh: 这个问题的一个近亲要回到第17部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设我们知道每个键被查找的频率。哪棵二叉搜索树能使期望查找代价最小？频繁的键应该靠近根，但树必须保持有序。<bookmark mark='b'/>递推式形状相同：对每个键的范围，尝试每个键作为根。立方时间。<bookmark mark='c'/>1971年，高德纳证明了：范围向右扩展时，最好的根从不向左移；向左扩展时，从不向右移。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以每个范围只需尝试两个邻居答案之间的根，总量降到平方。<bookmark mark='e'/>在两百个键时，同样的答案，步数少了三十三倍。它背后的不等式，后来叫作四边形不等式，能加速许多其他的动态规划。

d9fc09b032a9.en: Chapter thirteen. Dynamic programming on trees, graphs and sequences.
d9fc09b032a9.zh: 第13章。树、图与序列上的动态规划。

f54f86f8f7e6.en: On trees, the subproblems are subtrees. <bookmark mark='a'/> A company is planning a party. Each employee has a fun score, written in their circle, and nobody may be invited together with their direct boss. Who should come? <bookmark mark='b'/> This is the maximum-weight independent set, which is NP-hard on general graphs. On a tree it is easy. <bookmark mark='c'/> For each person compute two numbers, from the bottom of the tree up: the best total for their subtree if they come, and if they do not. <bookmark mark='d'/> If they come, their reports cannot; if they stay home, each report's subtree may do whichever is better. <bookmark mark='e'/> The best party here has a total of forty-seven, and a company of two hundred thousand takes a third of a second.
f54f86f8f7e6.zh: 在树上，子问题就是子树。<bookmark mark='a'/>一家公司在筹备聚会。每个员工有一个写在圆圈里的趣味分，任何人都不能和自己的直接上司同时被邀请。该邀请谁？<bookmark mark='b'/>这是最大权独立集，在一般图上是 NP 难的。在树上它很容易。<bookmark mark='c'/>对每个人，从树的底部向上算两个数：他来时其子树的最好总分，以及他不来时的。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果他来，他的下属就不能来；如果他不来，每个下属的子树可以取两者中较好的。<bookmark mark='e'/>这里最好的聚会总分是四十七，而一家二十万人的公司只要三分之一秒。

4268b0063df6.en: Several algorithms of Part 18 were dynamic programmes in disguise. <bookmark mark='a'/> Bellman–Ford's subproblems are the best paths using at most k edges; Floyd–Warshall's, the best paths through the first k vertices; Held–Karp's, the best path through a set of cities ending at a given one; and the longest path in a DAG, the best path ending at each vertex in topological order. <bookmark mark='b'/> Different subproblems, one method. <bookmark mark='c'/> Held–Karp shows the method's reach and its limit: sixteen cities in a little over a second, against six hundred and fifty billion tours by brute force. Still exponential, but exponentially better.
4268b0063df6.zh: 第18部分的好几个算法都是伪装起来的动态规划。<bookmark mark='a'/>贝尔曼–福特的子问题是至多 k 条边的最好路径；弗洛伊德–沃肖尔的是经过前 k 个顶点的最好路径；赫尔德–卡普的是经过一组城市、以给定城市结尾的最好路径；而有向无环图中的最长路径，是按拓扑顺序在每个顶点结尾的最好路径。<bookmark mark='b'/>子问题不同，方法一样。<bookmark mark='c'/>赫尔德–卡普展示了这个方法的威力和局限：十六个城市一秒多一点，而穷举要试六千五百亿条路线。仍然是指数的，但好了指数倍。

bc65583370d9.en: Sequences are dynamic programming's home ground. <bookmark mark='a'/> Andrew Viterbi's algorithm of 1967 finds the likeliest sequence of hidden states behind a sequence of observations, as a best path through a trellis; it decodes every mobile phone call, and AI, Built's seventh part used it for speech. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Cocke–Younger–Kasami algorithm decides whether a grammar can derive a string, using its substrings as subproblems, in cubic time, as Part 12 showed. <bookmark mark='c'/> Many dynamic programmes can be sped up when the table has structure, like Knuth's inequality: the convex-hull trick and divide-and-conquer optimization each shave a factor of n. <bookmark mark='d'/> The price of the method is memory for the table. Dan Hirschberg showed in 1975 that edit scripts can be recovered in linear space, combining dynamic programming with divide and conquer.
bc65583370d9.zh: 序列是动态规划的主场。<bookmark mark='a'/>安德鲁·维特比1967年的算法，把一串观测背后最可能的隐藏状态序列，作为穿过网格图的最好路径求出来；它为每一通手机通话解码，AI，从零构建的第七部分用它识别语音。<bookmark mark='b'/>Cocke–Younger–Kasami 算法以子串为子问题，在立方时间内判定一个文法能否推导出一个字符串，第12部分讲过。<bookmark mark='c'/>当表格有结构时，许多动态规划可以加速，就像高德纳的不等式：凸包技巧和分治优化各能省掉一个 n 的因子。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个方法的代价是表格的内存。丹·赫希伯格在1975年证明，编辑脚本可以在线性空间内恢复，把动态规划和分治结合了起来。

581313d07f5f.en: Chapter fourteen. Backtracking and Dancing Links.

92527aebcf89.en: When no clever structure is known, we search. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1848 the chess player Max Bezzel asked how to place eight queens on a chessboard so that none attacks another. <bookmark mark='b'/> Backtracking places one queen per row. In each row it tries the safe columns in turn; when a row has no safe column, it undoes the previous choice and moves that queen on. <bookmark mark='c'/> The power of the method is what it does not do: as soon as a partial placement fails, everything that would extend it is skipped. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here is the first solution found, and Franz Nauck showed in 1850 that there are ninety-two.
92527aebcf89.zh: 当没有已知的巧妙结构时，我们就搜索。<bookmark mark='a'/>1848年，国际象棋棋手马克斯·贝策尔问：怎样在棋盘上放八个皇后，使它们互不攻击？<bookmark mark='b'/>回溯每行放一个皇后。在每一行里依次尝试安全的列；当某一行没有安全的列时，就撤销上一个选择，把那个皇后往后移。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个方法的威力在于它不做的事：一旦部分放置失败，所有延伸它的放置都被跳过。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是找到的第一个解，而弗朗茨·瑙克在1850年证明了一共有九十二个。

e94f78a6fe85.en: Counted on this machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> For eight queens, backtracking visits two thousand and fifty-seven partial placements, out of almost seventeen million ways to put one queen in each row. <bookmark mark='b'/> But pruning does not change the nature of the problem: the search still grows exponentially, about five to six times per extra queen, and fourteen queens take twenty-seven million nodes and sixteen seconds, even with each node checked by a few bit operations.
e94f78a6fe85.zh: 在这台机器上计数。<bookmark mark='a'/>对八皇后，回溯访问了两千零五十七个部分放置，而每行放一个皇后的方法有近一千七百万种。<bookmark mark='b'/>但剪枝不改变问题的本质：搜索仍然指数增长，每多一个皇后大约变成五到六倍，十四个皇后要两千七百万个结点、十六秒，即使每个结点只用几次位运算检查。

5683ded74f8a.en: Sudoku is a better showcase. <bookmark mark='a'/> It is an exact cover problem: choose some rows of a zero–one matrix so that every column contains exactly one one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each row is a digit placed in a cell, seven hundred and twenty-nine of them, and each column is a constraint, three hundred and twenty-four: every cell filled, and every digit once in every row, column and box. <bookmark mark='c'/> Knuth's Algorithm X picks the constraint with the fewest options, tries each, deletes everything that conflicts with it, and recurses. <bookmark mark='d'/> The trick that makes it fast: to delete an element from a doubly linked list, point its neighbours at each other, but leave the element's own pointers alone. <bookmark mark='e'/> Then undoing is two assignments, and the element dances back into place. <bookmark mark='f'/> Backtracking restores the whole matrix in exactly the time it took to change it. Knuth named the technique dancing links in 2000, crediting Hitotumatu and Noshita, 1979.
5683ded74f8a.zh: 数独是更好的展示。<bookmark mark='a'/>它是一个精确覆盖问题：从一个零一矩阵中选出一些行，使每一列恰好有一个一。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一行是在某个格子里放某个数字，共七百二十九行；每一列是一个约束，共三百二十四列：每个格子都要填，每个数字在每行、每列、每个宫里各出现一次。<bookmark mark='c'/>高德纳的算法 X 选出选项最少的约束，逐一尝试，删去与它冲突的一切，再递归。<bookmark mark='d'/>让它变快的技巧：要从双向链表中删除一个元素，就让它的邻居互相指向，但保留这个元素自己的指针不动。<bookmark mark='e'/>于是撤销只要两次赋值，元素就跳着舞回到原位。<bookmark mark='f'/>回溯恢复整个矩阵所花的时间，恰好等于改变它所花的时间。高德纳在2000年把这个技术命名为舞蹈链，并归功于 Hitotumatu 和 Noshita 1979年的工作。

41d875a7ee72.en: Here is Arto Inkala's puzzle of 2012, often called the hardest Sudoku, with twenty-one givens, solved. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plain backtracking, filling cells in reading order, needed fifty thousand search nodes on it. Dancing links, always branching on the most constrained choice, needed under three thousand, and seventy milliseconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Most of the gain is the choice of what to branch on: fewest options first. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same engine tiles boards with pentominoes and solves scheduling puzzles, and Part 26 shows that Sudoku on larger boards is NP-complete, so nothing fundamentally better than clever search is expected. <bookmark mark='d'/> When the goal is the best solution rather than any, branch and bound adds an optimistic estimate to each node and prunes what cannot win, the method of Part 23's integer programs.
41d875a7ee72.zh: 这是阿尔托·因卡拉2012年的题目，常被称为最难的数独，有二十一个提示数，已经解出。<bookmark mark='a'/>朴素回溯按阅读顺序填格子，在它上面需要五万个搜索结点。舞蹈链总是在约束最强的选择上分支，只用了不到三千个，七十毫秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>大部分收益来自在什么上分支的选择：选项最少的优先。<bookmark mark='c'/>同样的引擎能用五格骨牌铺满棋盘、解决排程谜题，而第26部分会证明更大棋盘上的数独是 NP 完全的，所以不指望有根本上比聪明搜索更好的方法。<bookmark mark='d'/>当目标是最好的解而不是任意解时，分支定界给每个结点加上一个乐观估计，剪掉不可能获胜的部分，这是第23部分整数规划的方法。

60ed3bc3a600.en: Chapter fifteen. One problem, four paradigms.
60ed3bc3a600.zh: 第15章。一个问题，四种范式。

67c0d77fa008.en: To close the paradigms, one small problem solved four ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> Given a sequence of positive and negative numbers, which contiguous stretch has the largest sum? Here, the first six, adding to eighteen. <bookmark mark='b'/> Ulf Grenander at Brown University posed it in 1977, as a simplification of finding the brightest rectangle in a digitized picture. <bookmark mark='c'/> Jon Bentley told the story in his column Programming Pearls: within a short time it had four algorithms, each a different paradigm, and each asymptotically faster than the last.
67c0d77fa008.zh: 作为范式的收尾，用四种方法解决同一个小问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>给定一串正负数，哪一段连续的子数组和最大？这里是前六个，和为十八。<bookmark mark='b'/>布朗大学的乌尔夫·格雷南德在1977年提出了它，作为在数字化图片中寻找最亮矩形的简化版。<bookmark mark='c'/>乔恩·本特利在他的专栏《编程珠玑》中讲了这个故事：短时间内它就有了四个算法，各属一种范式，一个比一个渐近更快。

6e8925cbc719.en: The four. <bookmark mark='a'/> Brute force tries every start and every end, and adds up each stretch: cubic. <bookmark mark='b'/> Keeping a running sum while the end moves avoids re-adding: quadratic. <bookmark mark='c'/> Divide and conquer, Michael Shamos's: the best stretch lies in the left half, in the right half, or across the middle, and the best crossing one is found by scanning outwards in linear time. n log n, the recurrence of the closest pair. <bookmark mark='d'/> And dynamic programming, found by the statistician Jay Kadane, as Bentley tells it, within a minute of hearing the problem at a seminar: the best stretch ending at each position is either the number there alone, or the best stretch ending one earlier, extended. One pass, four lines.
6e8925cbc719.zh: 四个算法。<bookmark mark='a'/>穷举尝试每个起点和每个终点，并把每一段加起来：立方。<bookmark mark='b'/>在终点移动时保持一个累加和，就避免了重复相加：平方。<bookmark mark='c'/>分治，迈克尔·沙莫斯的方法：最好的一段要么在左半，要么在右半，要么跨过中间，而最好的跨中段可以从中间向外扫描在线性时间内求出。n log n，与最近点对同一个递推式。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有动态规划，据本特利所述，由统计学家杰伊·卡丹在一次研讨会上听到问题后不到一分钟就想出来：在每个位置结尾的最好一段，要么就是那里的数本身，要么是在前一个位置结尾的最好一段再延伸一格。一次扫描，四行代码。

456b4f9d28ce.en: Measured, the four separate like the curves of Part 16. <bookmark mark='a'/> The cubic method needs over half a second for four hundred numbers; on a million it would need centuries. <bookmark mark='b'/> The quadratic one takes five seconds for ten thousand. Divide and conquer handles a million numbers in six seconds, and Kadane's algorithm in under half a second. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the same machine, in the same language, the difference between the slowest and the fastest is not a constant factor. It is what can be done at all.
456b4f9d28ce.zh: 实测下来，四者像第16部分的曲线那样分开。<bookmark mark='a'/>立方方法处理四百个数就要半秒多；处理一百万个数要几个世纪。<bookmark mark='b'/>平方方法处理一万个数要五秒。分治处理一百万个数要六秒，卡丹的算法不到半秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>在同一台机器上、用同一种语言，最慢与最快之间的差别不是一个常数因子。它决定了什么事能做到。

8744137244fc.en: Chapter sixteen. Frontier: how fast can we multiply?
8744137244fc.zh: 第16章。前沿：乘法能有多快？

f925a7a2c99a.en: The first open question: is omega two? <bookmark mark='a'/> Every improvement since 1987 has applied Strassen's laser method to powers of one small tensor, Coppersmith and Winograd's. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2015 Andris Ambainis, Yuval Filmus and François Le Gall proved that this route cannot reach below two point three zero seven eight, however far it is pushed. <bookmark mark='c'/> Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams then showed similar limits for a much broader family of methods. <bookmark mark='d'/> So reaching two needs a new idea: perhaps Henry Cohn and Chris Umans's approach through group theory, or refinements like the asymmetric hashing behind the most recent gains. <bookmark mark='e'/> The stakes are wide: matrix multiplication sits inside linear algebra, finding triangles in graphs, transitive closure and context-free parsing.
f925a7a2c99a.zh: 第一个未解问题：omega 是二吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>1987年以来的每一次改进，都是把施特拉森的激光法用在一个小张量，即科珀史密斯–维诺格拉德张量的幂上。<bookmark mark='b'/>2015年，安德里斯·安拜尼斯、尤瓦尔·菲尔穆斯和弗朗索瓦·勒加尔证明了，无论推进多远，这条路都无法低于二点三零七八。<bookmark mark='c'/>乔希·阿尔曼和维尔吉尼娅·瓦西列夫斯卡·威廉斯随后对更广泛的一族方法证明了类似的极限。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以要达到二需要新的思想：也许是亨利·科恩和克里斯·乌曼斯借助群论的途径，或是像最近那些进展背后的非对称散列那样的改进。<bookmark mark='e'/>赌注很大：矩阵乘法位于线性代数、图中找三角形、传递闭包和上下文无关语法分析的内部。

421569ae4c96.en: The second: can edit distance beat chapter ten's quadratic table? <bookmark mark='a'/> The strong exponential time hypothesis, of Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, says that satisfiability with long clauses needs nearly two to the n time. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2015 Arturs Backurs and Piotr Indyk proved that a truly subquadratic algorithm for edit distance would refute it. <bookmark mark='c'/> The same was soon shown for the longest common subsequence and for dynamic time warping. <bookmark mark='d'/> These are conditional lower bounds: the best kind available, because proving unconditional ones for such problems is far beyond current techniques. This is fine-grained complexity, which Part 27 develops. <bookmark mark='e'/> Approximation escapes the barrier: in 2020 Alexandr Andoni and Negev Shekel Nosatzki computed edit distance to within a constant factor in almost linear time.
421569ae4c96.zh: 第二个：编辑距离能打败第10章的平方表格吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>拉塞尔·因帕利亚佐和拉马莫汉·帕图里的强指数时间假设说，子句很长的可满足性问题需要接近二的 n 次方的时间。<bookmark mark='b'/>2015年，阿图尔斯·巴库尔斯和彼得·因迪克证明了，编辑距离的真正次平方算法会推翻这个假设。<bookmark mark='c'/>不久，最长公共子序列和动态时间规整也被证明了同样的结论。<bookmark mark='d'/>这些是条件下界：现有的最好一种，因为为这类问题证明无条件的下界远远超出了当前的技术。这就是细粒度复杂性，第27部分会展开。<bookmark mark='e'/>近似可以绕开这道壁垒：2020年，亚历山大·安多尼和内盖夫·谢克尔·诺萨茨基在几乎线性的时间内把编辑距离算到了常数倍以内。

189e61368068.en: The third: is n log n the end for the FFT and for multiplication? <bookmark mark='a'/> Nobody knows an FFT with fewer than order n log n operations. <bookmark mark='b'/> Jacques Morgenstern proved in 1973 that n log n is necessary, but only for circuits whose constants are bounded, which leaves room for cleverness with large constants. <bookmark mark='c'/> For integer multiplication, Peyman Afshani, Casper Freksen, Lior Kamma and Kasper Green Larsen showed in 2019 that n log n is optimal, if a conjecture about information flow in networks is true. <bookmark mark='d'/> Unconditionally, no lower bound better than linear is known for either. The algorithms in this part may be optimal; nobody can prove it.
189e61368068.zh: 第三个：n log n 是 FFT 和乘法的终点吗？<bookmark mark='a'/>没有人知道运算次数少于 n log n 量级的 FFT。<bookmark mark='b'/>雅克·摩根斯滕在1973年证明 n log n 是必需的，但只针对常数有界的电路，这给使用大常数的巧思留下了余地。<bookmark mark='c'/>对整数乘法，佩曼·阿夫沙尼、卡斯珀·弗雷克森、利奥尔·卡马和卡斯珀·格林·拉森在2019年证明，如果一个关于网络中信息流的猜想成立，n log n 就是最优的。<bookmark mark='d'/>无条件地说，两者都没有已知的好于线性的下界。这一部分的算法也许是最优的；没人能证明。

71f2f57448f8.en: Here is where things stand. <bookmark mark='a'/> Is omega two, and is there any practical algorithm faster than Strassen's? <bookmark mark='b'/> Can edit distance be computed in truly subquadratic time, or can its hardness be proved without assuming SETH? <bookmark mark='c'/> Does every linear algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform need n log n operations? <bookmark mark='d'/> And which problems admit greedy algorithms? Matroids explain many, but not all: greedoids and other generalizations cover more. <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem takes the third.
71f2f57448f8.zh: 这就是现状。<bookmark mark='a'/>omega 是二吗？有没有比施特拉森更快的实用算法？<bookmark mark='b'/>编辑距离能在真正次平方的时间内计算吗？或者，能不借助强指数时间假设证明它的困难性吗？<bookmark mark='c'/>离散傅里叶变换的每个线性算法都需要 n log n 次运算吗？<bookmark mark='d'/>哪些问题有贪心算法？拟阵解释了许多，但不是全部：贪心拟阵和其他推广覆盖得更多。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题处理的是第三个。

ae48c8efff93.en: What we built in this part. Greedy algorithms and the exchange argument; Huffman codes; matroids and the theorem that says exactly when greedy works. Karatsuba's three products and Strassen's seven. The fast Fourier transform, from the roots of unity to butterflies, and the multiplication of million-digit numbers. The closest pair. Dynamic programming, from Fibonacci through edit distance, knapsack, matrix chains, search trees and trees. Backtracking and dancing links. And one problem solved four ways.
ae48c8efff93.zh: 这一部分我们造了什么。贪心算法与交换论证；哈夫曼编码；拟阵，以及准确刻画贪心何时有效的定理。Karatsuba 的三次乘法和施特拉森的七次。快速傅里叶变换，从单位根到蝶形，以及百万位数的乘法。最近点对。动态规划，从斐波那契到编辑距离、背包、矩阵链、搜索树和树。回溯与舞蹈链。以及用四种方法解决的同一个问题。

ece6b138a313.en: Where this comes back. Part 20 adds a fifth paradigm, randomness. Part 21 turns edit distance into diff, a shortest path on the edit graph. Part 23 is linear programming and branch and bound. Part 26 proves that knapsack, subset sum and Sudoku are NP-complete, and Part 27 develops the fine-grained complexity behind edit distance's quadratic barrier. Part 30's cryptography runs on big-number arithmetic, and Part 53's quantum computers run the FFT's butterfly on amplitudes.
ece6b138a313.zh: 这些会在哪里再出现。第20部分加入第五种范式：随机性。第21部分把编辑距离变成 diff，即编辑图上的一条最短路径。第23部分是线性规划和分支定界。第26部分证明背包、子集和与数独是 NP 完全的，第27部分发展编辑距离平方壁垒背后的细粒度复杂性。第30部分的密码学运行在大数算术上，第53部分的量子计算机在振幅上运行 FFT 的蝶形。

b11dbc645a8b.en: In practice. Fourier transforms run in every phone, camera, radio and audio codec, through libraries such as FFTW and cuFFT. Big-number libraries such as GMP switch from the school method to Karatsuba, Toom–Cook and the FFT at sizes tuned for each machine. Matrix libraries stay cubic, but blocked and vectorized; Strassen is rare. Diff, spell checkers and DNA aligners are dynamic programmes, and SAT, integer programming and constraint solvers are search with very clever pruning.
b11dbc645a8b.zh: 在实践中。傅里叶变换通过 FFTW 和 cuFFT 这样的库，运行在每一部手机、相机、收音机和音频编解码器里。GMP 这样的大数库会在为每台机器调好的规模上，从学校方法切换到 Karatsuba、Toom–Cook 和 FFT。矩阵库保持立方，但做了分块和向量化；施特拉森很少用。diff、拼写检查器和 DNA 比对器是动态规划，而 SAT、整数规划和约束求解器是剪枝非常巧妙的搜索。

2e90f261699e.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: the number-theoretic transform in the Pebble language, multiplying five-hundred-digit numbers on the emulator. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
2e90f261699e.zh: 六道习题，完整的解答在这一部分的讲义里。在任何一道上都可以暂停。第五道是动手题：用 Pebble 语言实现数论变换，在模拟器上做五百位数的乘法。最后一道标着星号，是研究题：它的答案还不知道，讲义里说了从哪里开始。

371ebec2681b.en: Next time, a fifth paradigm. A coin flip can stand in for cleverness: checking a matrix product in n squared time, finding a minimum cut by contracting random edges, testing primes in milliseconds, and counting the top words of the thirty novels in a few kilobytes, the ledger's ninth row. Part 20, Randomness as a Resource.
371ebec2681b.zh: 下一次，第五种范式。抛一枚硬币可以代替聪明：在 n 的平方时间内检验一个矩阵乘积，通过随机收缩边找到最小割，在几毫秒内检验素数，以及用几千字节统计三十部小说中最常见的词，即账本的第九行。第20部分，作为资源的随机性。
